sections.timeline: Patient ate shellfish about 20 minutes prior to EMS arrival. Started getting pale and sweaty, chest tightened, then fell over unresponsive. Fire arrived, found no pulse, started compressions and applied AED. AED advised no shock, then later advised shock, which was delivered. Patient then had an allergic reaction to shellfish, with swelling in airway and hives, difficulty breathing. BP 140/90. Patient reported mild reactions to shellfish previously, but this is the first severe reaction. Patient does not carry an EpiPen. Patient reported pain as 'hard to breathe and itchy'. Patient then had a dirt bike accident, with a twisted leg and obvious deformity of the femur. Patient reported pain as a 6/10, like 'bones in half'. Patient was dizzy and nauseous. Pedal pulse present. Patient reported hitting head, but no neck or back pain.

sections.narrative: Fire and EMS responded to a call for an allergic reaction at 123 Fake Street. Patient Dave, 18, ate shellfish about 20 minutes prior and developed swelling in his airway, hives, and difficulty breathing. BP was 140/90. Patient reported previous mild reactions to shellfish but this was the first severe one, and he does not carry an EpiPen. Later, patient Dave was involved in a dirt bike accident, sustaining a deformed femur and reporting pain as 6/10. He was dizzy and nauseous, but had a pedal pulse.
